what_it_does: Compiling an AI model — translating a high-level description of a neural network into efficient machine instructions — is tricky when the shapes of the data being processed are not known until the program actually runs (for example, because user inputs have varying lengths, as with text in a language model). Existing compilers treat three different levels of the program — the overall network graph, the low-level mathematical kernels (small programs that run on the GPU to compute one operation), and calls to hand-optimized external math libraries — as separate worlds that cannot optimize across each other's boundaries. Relax introduces a single unified intermediate representation (a common language that describes all three levels) used throughout the Apache TVM compiler. It attaches symbolic shape labels to every operation, so the compiler can reason about varying sizes across the whole program at once. This enables optimizations that were previously impossible, such as fusing operators across abstraction levels and generating code that works on phones, microcontrollers, and web browsers in addition to desktop GPUs.
